# Mahāpalobhanajātaka (Ja 507)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul14.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāpalobhanajātaka* (Ja 507) is a canonical birth-story included in the Pali *Jātaka* collection. The story is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers it in connection with the defilement of pure beings by women, addressed to a dissatisfied monk (*ukkhaṇṭhitabhikkhu*) who attains arahantship upon hearing the teaching [Fausböll 1887]. Opening with the verse cue *Brahmalokā cavitvānā*, the story recounts a previous existence in which the Bodhisatta, having passed away from the Brahma realm, took rebirth as a royal prince surrounded by palace luxury [Collins 1998; Fausböll 1887]. Because sensual desire does not exist in the Brahma worlds, he maintained an aversion to sensual pleasures and refused all contact with women, earning the name Prince Aniṭṭhigandha ("one who has no smell for women") [Collins 1998; Fausböll 1887]. In the conclusion, after withstanding attempts at seduction, he renounced household life for an ascetic hermitage in the forest (*araññe isipabbajjam*), eliminated sensual attachment (*kāmarāgaṃ virājetvā*), and returned to the Brahma realm [Fausböll 1887].
